newsitem.title: USA: USDA's Collins - EEP use more likely this summer.
newsitem.headline: USDA's Collins - EEP use more likely this summer.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department chief economist Keith Collins Tuesday said tight world wheat stocks and high prices made use of the Export Enhancement Program unlikely at this time but said the picture may be different this summer.

Testifying before the House Agriculture Committee, Collins noted U.S. wheat prices received by farmers averaged about $4 per bushel in January. But he said there were prospects for prices to come down.

Collins said the key indicators for a restart of the U.S. subsidy program would be the pattern of European Union subsidies, the pattern of aggressive sales by other competitors and the size of the U.S. July wheat crop.
He said if that crop came in "quite strong" and the U.S. market share should start to erode, "that presents a much different picture than what we see now."
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman also told the House panel he was concerned about EU subsidies on wheat flour and said the United States would use wheat flour subsidies if necessary.
